paragraphs: In the morning, prepare shampoo, towels, and disinfectant. After opening, sequence clients by appointment, support each head while rinsing, apply product, and massage while checking the pressure. Take extra care with sensitive scalps, then guide clients to styling chairs and hand them off to hairstylists. Between clients, wipe surfaces and wash towels. Work continuously through midday and evening peaks, then clean and disinfect before closing.

In short: wash clients' hair comfortably and massage them into relaxation. Duties include adjusting water temperature, rinsing and shampooing, scalp massage, scalp observation, guidance and handoffs, plus cleaning and disinfection. Using both hands and communication, shampooers create the first stage of the salon experience.

AI will not replace shampooers because this is a fully hands-on, close-contact service role that depends on touch. Systems take over appointments and membership reminders, but shampooing and massage cannot be automated in the near term. The real concern is the occupation's low entry barrier and easy replacement by new workers, not machines taking the work.

Moderately high exposure does not mean high risk. Appointment recordkeeping is being replaced, not the hands that wash hair. The true pressure comes from low entry barriers and high turnover, not machines. Developing renowned technique and service creates greater stability.
